suite: Cornered by a serial killer who hurt my family, holding a weapon
nightmare: I’m backed into the corner of my childhood kitchen, the yellow light buzzing overhead, and he’s standing in the doorway with that same knife glinting in his hand, his boots leaving dark wet prints across the tile. I can smell metal and bleach and something rotten, and somewhere behind me I hear my mother crying and my little brother making these broken choking sounds, like they’re close but I can’t get to them. He keeps smiling at me like he already knows I can’t move, and every time I try to scream my throat locks up while the blade scrapes slowly along the wall beside my face. He takes one step closer, then another, raising the knife as I feel the cold cabinets digging into my back, and I know he’s about to do to me what he already did to them.

tests.input: I lunge out of the corner before he can get closer, slam both hands into his chest, and knock the knife out of his grip. I pin him to the floor and get past the doorway.
When he raises the blade, I catch his wrist with both hands and twist hard until he drops it. I don't freeze this time—I drive him back and take control of the room.
I push myself up straight, stop shrinking into the cabinets, and hit him before he reaches me. He looks surprised, and I keep moving until he's the one backing away.
I finally get my voice back and scream for help as loud as I can, banging on the wall and yelling the neighbors' names. People start pounding on the front door and he hesitates.
Instead of staying trapped, I call out to my mother and hear her answer me clearly from the next room. We move toward each other, and once we're together I don't feel alone with him anymore.
My little brother appears beside me, breathing normally, and takes my hand while I shout for someone to call the police. The kitchen fills with people coming to help us.
I reach onto the counter, grab a heavy cast-iron pan, and hold it between us like a shield. When he steps in, I swing it and make enough space to get to the door.
I realize the back door is right beside the sink, and I slip past the table and throw it open. Cold air rushes in, and I get out of the kitchen before he can touch me.

The yellow buzzing light suddenly becomes clear daylight, and the whole kitchen looks clean and ordinary instead of rotten. The knife in his hand is just a dull butter knife, and he can't scare me anymore.
I feel my throat loosening when I take one slow breath and then another. My body settles down enough for me to think, and the panic stops running everything.
I look at him and realize he's feeding off my fear, so I let the fear drop instead of fighting it. Once I feel steady inside, he doesn't seem bigger than me anymore.
I stop trying to force a scream and just ground myself, feeling my feet on the tile and my back against the cabinets. Then my voice comes back naturally, clear and strong.
When he lifts the knife, I hold up my hand and it freezes in the air like time stopped around it. He can't move another inch while I walk past him.
I say one word and his whole body unravels into black smoke that gets pulled into the vent. The kitchen goes quiet, and the danger is just gone.
A bright gold light comes out of my chest and fills the whole kitchen, and nothing violent can cross it. He tries to step toward me, but the light throws him back and shields my family too.
I slide down into the corner and pull my knees up tight, trying to make myself as small and quiet as I can. I keep my eyes on the floor and wait for him to pass me by.
I don't move at all when he comes closer, not even when the knife lifts. My whole body just locks and I stand there like if I stay still enough, maybe he won't notice me.
I drop to the floor and crawl behind the table and cabinets, covering my head with my arms. I can still hear my mother crying, but I stay hidden and don't go toward them.
Right when he raises the knife, I force my eyes open and drag myself out of the dream. I wake up hard and fast before anything else can happen.
I tell myself this has to stop and the whole thing just cuts off. Suddenly I'm awake in bed, breathing hard, and none of it gets resolved.
As soon as I hear my brother choking, I pinch myself and yank myself out of it. I leave the kitchen completely by waking up before he reaches me.
I grab the knife out of his hand and drive it into him over and over, way past what's needed. I don't stop until he's on the floor and the whole kitchen is covered in blood.
I rush him and smash his face into the cabinets, then keep beating him until I feel his bones give. I want him to suffer the whole time and know exactly why it's happening.
I take the knife and slice him apart piece by piece, and then I start tearing up the kitchen too. Nothing is left standing by the time I'm done with him.
He's standing there with the knife and I just feel blank. My mother is crying and my brother is choking, but none of it touches me.
I look at him and realize I'm not scared at all, just flat and calm like it doesn't matter. Even with everything in the kitchen, I tell myself I'm fine and it means nothing.
I hear the sounds behind me and smell the blood and bleach, but I shrug it off like it's no big deal. I don't care what happened to them or what he's about to do to me.
It all plays out exactly the way it always does. I'm still trapped in the kitchen, he still comes closer with the knife, and I still can't get to my family.
Nothing changes in the dream. The light buzzes, the smell hits me, my throat locks up, and he raises the knife while I stand there helpless.

I relive the whole thing exactly as it happened before, down to his wet footprints on the tile and my mother's crying behind me. He smiles, takes those same steps toward me, and I'm stuck waiting for it.
I’m terrified and completely frozen, like the fear is filling up my whole body and I can’t even breathe right. My chest is tight and I feel helpless.
I feel this horrible dread in my stomach, like I already know something unbearable is coming. I’m panicked, sick, and so small.
I’m scared to the point of going numb. There’s this heavy helpless feeling in me, like my voice and my body have both shut down.
The kitchen is washed in that dull yellow light, and it makes everything look dirty and wrong. The air feels sharp and chemical, like bleach and metal are stuck in the room.
It’s a cramped old kitchen with cold tile and hard cabinets pressed behind me. The whole place feels close and airless, and the buzzing overhead never stops.
The floor has dark wet footprints across it, and the room smells rotten underneath the bleach. Everything is too quiet except for the faint crying and that low electrical hum.
I wrench the knife away and go at him hard enough that he finally drops, and I keep hitting until I'm sure he can't come after me or my family again.
I just stand there shaking and feeling the panic flood my whole body, like all I can do is notice how scared and trapped I am.
I tell myself to stay calm and not let the fear in, so I kind of shut it off and keep my face blank while he comes closer.
It all unfolds the same way in that kitchen, with the light buzzing and the knife catching the yellow glare, like I'm just watching the exact scene happen again.
I slip past him and get out of the kitchen as fast as I can, not really to fight him but at least to stop standing there pinned in that corner.
I tell myself this doesn't get to keep happening and try to break whatever is going on, like either I change it or force myself out of it somehow.

I mean, this still feels kind of fake to me, but fine, instead of freezing I yell for my mom and brother, grab the heavy chair by the table, and wedge it between me and the knife so I can get us out the back door.
I’m so panicked I can barely think, and instead of doing anything I just slide down behind the kitchen table and stay hidden there until I wake myself up.
I try to slow my breathing and tell myself he can’t control me, but the second he steps closer with the knife I give up and force myself awake before anything else happens.
I honestly don’t get how rewriting this is supposed to help, because all I want to do is crawl under the sink cabinet and make myself disappear until he’s gone.
I’m terrified, but I make myself take one full breath, plant my feet, and shout for my brother to come to me while I grab the bleach bottle and use it to distract him so we can run.
I steady myself first so my voice works again, then I call to my mom and brother, pull open the back door, and we move together out of the kitchen while I keep the chair between us and him.

suite: Fighting a regenerating demon that requires total destruction to stop
nightmare: I’m in a burned-out church with black smoke hanging in the air, and this thing is crawling toward me on too many limbs, its skin splitting open to show wet red muscle that knits itself back together every time I hack at it. The sound is the worst part—bones cracking back into place, meat slithering and sealing, and this deep, choking laugh coming from its throat while my hands slip on the handle of the axe because they’re slick with blood and sweat. I can smell sulfur and rot, and every time I tear off a piece of it, another hand or jaw pushes out of the wound, reaching for me, faster now, like it’s learning how afraid I am. I back into the altar and realize there are still pieces of it twitching all around me, pulling themselves together from the floor, and when all of its faces turn toward me at once and start rushing me, I can’t lift my arms anymore.

tests.input: I stop backing up and plant my feet at the altar, then I grip the axe with both hands and drive it straight into its chest until it finally drops. When the other pieces start pulling together, I keep moving toward them instead of freezing.
I shove the creature away hard enough to make space, and I go after its legs so it can't keep crawling at me. Once it falls, I pin it down and hold my ground.
When all the faces turn toward me, I rush it first. I swing cleanly and keep attacking with purpose, like my body finally works and I know exactly what to do.
I yell for help and my voice actually carries through the church. A group of people comes through the side doors and stands beside me so I'm not alone with it anymore.
I call out for my brother, and he appears near the front pews and grabs my arm. He helps me get steady and tells me we're getting out of this together.
Instead of trying to handle it by myself, I shout to the people in the church to help me. They start pulling me back from the altar and one of them takes the axe while another opens a way out.

I reach up and pull a chain above the altar, and the whole sprinkler system comes on. The water and bright light wash the smoke out, and the thing starts shrinking until it's weak enough to deal with.
I notice a side door behind the choir stalls and head for it instead of staying trapped at the altar. Once I push it open, clean air comes in and the creature can't follow me outside.

I grab one of the heavy candlesticks and slam it into the floor, and the church starts changing around me. The black smoke clears, sunlight comes through the windows, and the thing looks smaller and less powerful in the open light.
I make myself take one slow breath and then another, and my hands stop slipping. Once I calm down, I can think clearly enough to move instead of panic.
I look at it and feel the fear come up, but I tell myself I'm not helpless and it doesn't control me. That thought takes some of its power away, and my body loosens enough for me to act.
The choking laugh starts again, and instead of spiraling I get really calm. I know I can handle what's in front of me, and the dream stops feeling like it's swallowing me.
I lift my hand and this bright white light pours out of it across the church. Wherever it touches the creature, the extra limbs and faces dissolve until there's nothing left to come at me.
Right when it rushes me, my body turns strong and almost made of metal, so it can't tear into me at all. I feel invincible, and it starts backing away from me instead.
I rise up off the floor and float above the altar while the broken pieces of it claw at empty air. From up there I send down fire from my hands and the whole thing burns away.
I drop behind the altar and curl up tight, trying not to breathe too loud while it crawls past. I just stay there and hope it doesn't notice me.
When all the faces turn toward me, I go completely still and stop fighting. I can't make myself run or swing, so I just stand there and let it come closer.
I lie down in the ash and blood and pretend I'm already dead. I keep my eyes shut and wait for it to lose interest.
Right before it reaches me, I force my eyes open and rip myself out of sleep. I don't stay there long enough to see what happens.
I tell myself to wake up and the whole church cuts out at once. Everything just stops before it touches me.
As soon as I feel trapped against the altar, I start thrashing until I wake up in bed. The dream doesn't really resolve, it just breaks off.
I go at it with the axe until I'm chopping through every face and limb over and over, long after it stops moving. I don't just kill it, I reduce it to a pile of wet pieces.
I pin it in the pews and set the whole church on fire so it can scream while it burns. I keep feeding the flames until there's nothing left but blackened meat and ash.
I smash each twitching part of it one by one, stomping on the hands and jaws as they try to regrow. I make sure every last scrap is destroyed.
It's all still there—the smoke, the rot, the cracking bones—but I don't feel anything about it. I'm just blank, like none of it matters.
I watch it come toward me and I tell myself I'm fine, totally fine. The fear doesn't count and I act like it doesn't bother me at all.
The blood on my hands and the smell of sulfur are there, but I stay flat and cold the whole time. I don't let myself react because I don't care what happens.
It happens exactly the same way as always. I'm in the burned church, I hack at it, it keeps growing back, and I end up trapped at the altar unable to move.
Nothing is different. The creature keeps coming, the sound gets worse, the pieces on the floor pull themselves back together, and I freeze when it rushes me.
I just relive the whole thing straight through without changing anything. All of its faces turn toward me at once and I still can't lift my arms when it comes.
I feel pure terror in my chest, like I can't breathe and my whole body knows I'm about to die. I'm helpless and frozen watching it come closer.
I'm so scared I can't move. It feels like all the strength drains out of me and I'm just trapped there in panic.
I feel sickened and terrified at the same time, and the dread just keeps building. There's this awful helpless feeling, like nothing I do would matter.
The church is burned black, with heavy smoke hanging in the air and a strong smell of sulfur and rot. Everything looks scorched and ruined around the altar.
The whole place is filled with those wet, cracking noises, and the air feels thick and hard to breathe. Blood is smeared across the floor among the broken pieces.
It's dim and smoky inside, and the altar behind me feels cold and damaged. Pieces of the creature are twitching all over the ground in the ruined church.

I swing the axe into it over and over and keep chopping at whatever grows back until it finally stops coming at me. It feels like I'm just trying to survive, but I don't really stop once I've started.
I just stand there shaking, like my body won't listen, and all I can think is how scared I am. Part of me is feeling the fear, but part of me is almost giving up and not doing anything.
I tell myself not to let it get to me and keep my face blank while it comes closer. I'm calmer on the surface, though I might just be shoving the fear down so I can keep going.

It's the same burned church, the same smell, the same thing pulling itself together and coming at me again. I'm mostly just describing it, but it also feels like I'm right back inside the exact nightmare.
I move away from it fast and try to get out from in front of the altar before it reaches me. It could be me taking charge of the situation, or maybe I'm just trying not to face it.

I tell myself this has to stop and force everything in me toward changing what's happening right there. It sounds like taking control, but it also feels a little like trying to shut the whole dream off.

This whole rewrite thing feels kind of fake to me, but okay, instead of hacking at it I plant my feet at the altar, grab the brass cross stand, and pin its limbs down while I shout for people to come help me.
I'm honestly terrified because it keeps growing back and learning me, so I just panic and force myself awake before it reaches the altar.

I take a breath and tell myself it's just trying to feed on my fear, and for a second I back toward the church doors like I'm going to face it calmly, but then I lose it and bolt out and hide behind the pews until it's gone.
I don't really get how making this up is supposed to help, and honestly I just crawl under the altar and stay completely still so none of its faces can find me.
I'm scared as hell when all the faces turn toward me, but I slow my breathing, stop swinging wildly, and tell it out loud it doesn't get to decide what happens in this church.

I steady my hands first so I'm not slipping on the axe anymore, then I ring the church bell and people come in with extinguishers and heavy blankets and we trap the thing before it can pull itself back together.

suite: Paralyzed on train tracks with a train approaching fast
nightmare: I’m lying flat on cold train tracks at night, my cheek pressed against the greasy metal rail, and no matter how hard I try, I can’t move anything but my eyes. In the distance I see a single white headlight swelling larger and larger, and I hear the train horn blare through the dark, mixed with the violent rattle of the tracks vibrating under my body so hard it feels like my bones are shaking loose. I try to scream, but my throat only makes this thin, broken sound, and I can smell hot metal and dirt while the light floods over me and the engine rushes closer impossibly fast. Right before it reaches me, the whole world is nothing but deafening noise, blinding light, and the certainty that I’m about to be crushed.

tests.input: I force my arms to work all at once, shove myself sideways, and roll off the rails into the gravel before the train reaches me. I’m breathing hard, but I’m on my feet and out of its path.
Instead of freezing, I jerk upright and step off the tracks on my own. I square my shoulders and watch the train blast past without touching me.
I dig my elbows into the ground and drag myself forward until my body finally breaks free of the rails. Once I’m clear, I keep moving until I know I’m safe.
My voice comes back enough for me to yell, and people from the station run toward me. Two of them grab my arms and pull me off the tracks together.
I manage to wave one hand, and the engineer notices me through the headlight. The horn changes, the brakes scream, and the train stops short while workers rush out to help me.
Out of nowhere my brother is there beside me, telling me to look at him and keep breathing. He hauls me up under the shoulders and gets me off the rails just in time.
I notice a shallow maintenance trench beside the track and drop into it. The train roars over me, but I’m protected underneath and come out shaken but okay.
There’s a heavy track switch next to me, and I grab it and throw all my weight into it. The train gets diverted onto the other line and misses me completely.
The tracks start changing under me until I realize I’m actually lying on an empty station platform, not in danger at all. The train just pulls in normally and stops to let me step aboard.
I stop fighting the panic and take one slow, full breath. As soon as I calm down, my body loosens and I can move myself off the tracks.
I feel the fear, but I tell myself I’m not helpless and the terror starts to shrink. Once I believe that, the paralysis breaks and I move with a clear head.
The light gets bigger, but I stay surprisingly calm and grounded instead of spiraling. That calm gives me enough control to roll away before the train arrives.
Right before the train hits me, my body lifts straight up into the air like gravity stops working. I hover above the tracks and watch it pass underneath me.
I throw out my hand and the whole train locks in place a few feet from me, silent and still. Then I stand up and walk away from it.
As the engine comes at me, I turn into a bright streak of light and slip off the tracks instantly. The train can’t touch me because I’m not trapped in a body anymore.
I stop fighting and just lie perfectly still on the tracks, staring up at the light and hoping if I don't move at all maybe it somehow passes over me.
I squeeze my eyes shut and go limp, like if I don't look at it and don't make a sound, I can disappear into the dark until it's over.
I can't get off the rails, so I just fold in on myself as much as I can and stay frozen there, trying not to draw any attention while the train gets closer.
Right when the headlight hits my face, I force my eyes open and yank myself awake before anything happens.
As soon as I hear the horn, I tell myself this isn't real and I rip out of the dream and wake up in bed.
I can feel the tracks shaking under me, and instead of staying there I make myself bolt awake so the whole scene just cuts off.
I suddenly rip free, jump up, and tear the train apart with my bare hands, crushing the engine and smashing metal until there's nothing left but twisted wreckage.
I stop the train, drag the conductor out, and beat him to death on the tracks because I want him to suffer the way I was about to.
The fear flips into rage and I make the whole train explode, cars flying everywhere, fire everywhere, everybody inside getting wiped out with it.
I'm still lying on the tracks with the train coming, but I don't feel scared or upset about it at all. It doesn't matter to me.
The light gets bigger and the rails are shaking, and I'm just blank about it, like none of it touches me and I'm completely fine.
I watch the train rushing at me and honestly I don't care. It's like my body is there, but emotionally I have nothing to say about it.
It goes exactly the same way every time: I'm stuck on the tracks, the horn blares, the light fills everything, and I know I'm about to be crushed.
I try to move and can't, I try to scream and barely make a sound, and the train keeps coming just like before with nothing different.
I'm back with my cheek on the cold rail, smelling the metal and dirt, hearing that same horn, and it all happens the same until the moment right before impact.
I’m completely terrified, like every part of me is locked up with panic and I know something awful is coming. The fear is so big it almost blots everything else out.
I feel helpless and trapped, and this heavy dread keeps building in my chest as the sound gets closer. It’s that sick certainty that I’m not going to get away.
I’m so scared I feel tiny, like I don’t matter against something huge bearing down on me. There’s this raw helplessness and horror all through me.
It’s nighttime and the tracks are freezing under my face, with grease and dirt pressed into my skin. The whole place feels dark, empty, and exposed.
There’s a single white light far off in the dark, and it keeps looking brighter against everything around it. The rails hum and the air smells like hot metal.
The night around me is black and barren, and the tracks are vibrating with this harsh, rattling noise. The horn cuts through the dark and the whole scene feels cold and brutal.
At the last second I somehow wrench one arm free and slam at the front of the train with everything I've got, like I'm trying to stop it or smash it away before it hits me.
I just lie there feeling completely terrified, and all I can do is stare at the light and hear myself making these weak little sounds.
I tell myself not to panic and sort of press the fear down so I can stay calm while the train keeps coming.
It's the same cold tracks, the same horn, the same light getting bigger, and it all plays out the way it always does.
As soon as I can move, I throw myself off the tracks and get as far from the rail as I can before the train reaches me.
I tell myself this doesn't get to keep happening and I force everything in me to break the scene somehow, like either changing it or jerking myself out of it.
This whole rewriting thing feels kind of fake to me, but fine, I picture myself slowing my breathing, rolling my body off the rail, and standing up beside the tracks before the train gets there.
I’m so scared when I hear the train coming that instead of doing anything I just force myself awake right before it hits me.
I tell myself to stay calm and yank my arm enough to start sliding off the track, but then I panic and just blank the whole dream out so it ends.
I honestly don't get how this is supposed to help, and in the rewrite I just drag myself under the platform and hide there until everything passes.
I’m still really scared, but I make myself breathe, yell for the conductor to stop, and pull my body off the tracks instead of freezing there.
I steady myself first so I’m not trapped in that panic, and then I grab the signal lever by the tracks and wave down help so the train stops before it reaches me.

suite: Trapped in a room full of snakes with severe phobia
nightmare: I’m standing in a small, windowless room with damp concrete walls, and the floor is moving before I realize it’s covered in snakes, thick and thin bodies sliding over each other with a wet, whispering sound that fills the air. The smell is sour and earthy, and I can feel my throat tightening as cold scales brush against my bare feet and begin winding around my ankles; every time I jerk away, there are more of them, coiling out of the corners and dropping from the ceiling vents. I’m pounding on the locked door, screaming so hard my chest burns, but all I can hear over my own voice is the constant hissing and the soft slap of bodies against the floor as they rise higher around my legs. Then I look down and see one lifting its head right in front of my face, its tongue flicking against my skin as the mass of them tightens around me and I can’t move at all.

tests.input: I stop pounding on the door and start stamping hard, kicking the snakes away from my legs until there’s space around me. Then I grab the one in front of my face by the neck and throw it across the room.
Instead of freezing, I plant my feet and ram my shoulder into the door over and over until the lock gives. I shove through it before the snakes can pull me back down.
I turn toward the snakes and hold my ground instead of panicking. I use my hands to peel them off my ankles and keep pushing them back until they stop closing in on me.
I yell for my partner, and suddenly they’re on the other side of the door telling me to keep talking to them. They get it open and pull me out while I hold onto their arm.
I scream for help and this time people actually hear me. Two workers rush in with boots and gloves and guide me through the snakes to the hallway.
When I call out, my mother appears calm and steady, and she tells me to look at her and keep breathing. She takes my hand and walks me to the door, and the snakes back away from us.
I notice a metal pipe hanging loose under the vent, so I wrench it free and use it to sweep the snakes back. That gives me enough room to reach the lock and get out.
I see a floor hatch in the corner that wasn’t obvious at first, and I pry it open. There’s a narrow stairway underneath, so I climb down and leave the room behind me.
I find a switch on the wall and flip on bright lights and a loud fan. Once the room is clear, I can see they’re small harmless garter snakes, and they scatter away from my feet.
I make myself take one slow breath and then another, and my chest stops burning. When I stop thrashing, I can think clearly enough to step carefully and keep the snakes from wrapping tighter.
I look at the room and tell myself I’m scared, but I’m not helpless. As soon as I believe that, the panic drops and the snakes lose some of their grip on me.
I stop screaming and focus on staying calm, almost like grounding myself inside the dream. The hissing fades into the background, and I’m able to move without feeling trapped.
I lift my hand and everything in the room goes still, like I can control it with a thought. The snakes freeze in place long enough for me to walk right through them.
Wings come out of my back and I lift up off the floor before the snakes can reach me. I fly straight through the ceiling vent into open air.
My whole body starts glowing hot, and the snakes can’t hold onto me anymore. I turn into fire and the coils fall away while I move through the locked door like it’s nothing.
I pull my knees up and press myself against the wall, trying not to move at all so maybe the snakes will lose interest. I keep my eyes shut and just wait for it to be over.
I cover my face with my hands and stand completely still while they slide over my legs. I tell myself if I don't react, nothing worse will happen.
I lower myself onto the concrete and go limp like I'm dead, barely breathing while the snakes coil around me. I don't fight them anymore, I just let them be there.
Right before the snake gets to my face, I force myself awake and sit up gasping. I don't stay in the room long enough to see what happens next.
I just make the whole thing stop and everything goes black. Then I'm awake in bed before the snakes can reach any higher.
I realize it's happening and I pinch myself hard until I wake up. The room and the hissing disappear, but nothing actually gets resolved.
I grab a machete from nowhere and start chopping the snakes apart, over and over until the floor is covered in blood and pieces of them. I don't stop until every last one is shredded.
I set the whole room on fire and listen to them sizzle while they twist around in the flames. I want all of them destroyed, even if the whole place burns down with them.
I start stomping on their heads and smashing them into the concrete until they're pulp. I keep going in this rage, killing them in the most brutal way I can.
The snakes are all over me, but I don't feel scared or grossed out by it at all. I just stand there like it means nothing.
I look down at them wrapping around my legs and I shrug because it doesn't bother me. Even the hissing in my face feels unimportant, like I don't care either way.
I keep telling myself I'm fine, totally calm, and none of this is getting to me. The room is full of snakes, but emotionally I feel absolutely nothing.

It's the exact same room, the same smell, the same snakes covering the floor and dropping from the vents. I pound on the locked door, they wrap around my legs, and I end up stuck again with one right in my face.
Nothing changes at all. I feel the cold scales on my feet, I panic, more snakes keep coming, and I can't move while they tighten around me.
I go through the whole thing exactly like before, screaming at the door while the hissing gets louder and louder. It still ends with me frozen in place, surrounded and unable to get away.
I feel absolutely terrified, like my whole body is frozen and my chest is going to cave in from panic.
I’m so scared and helpless that it feels like all the strength drains out of me at once. There’s this awful sense that I’m completely trapped.
I feel sick with dread, and this deep disgust crawls through me at the same time. It’s like fear is sitting in my throat and I can barely breathe around it.
The room is small and windowless, with damp concrete walls and a sour, earthy smell hanging in the air.
The floor is covered in thick and thin snakes sliding over each other, and the whole space is filled with hissing and that wet slapping sound.
The air feels tight and stale, and everything around me seems close and oppressive. Cold scales brush against my bare skin while the room stays dim and closed in.

I start kicking and stomping at the snakes around my feet, and when one lifts up near my face I grab it and slam it away hard enough that the rest back off. I can't tell if I'm just trying to get free or if I'm going further than I need to.

I just stand there shaking and feel the panic take over, like my body won't do anything except stare at them and breathe too fast. Part of me is letting myself feel how scared I am, but part of me is just not acting at all.

I tell myself to stay calm and not give the fear any more room, so I kind of push it down and focus on getting through it. It feels steadying, but also a little like I'm refusing to feel what's actually there.

It's the same windowless room and the snakes keep coming out of the corners and vents just like before, and I watch it happen again. I'm not really changing anything, just describing it as it repeats.
I start moving fast toward the door, trying to get my legs free and put distance between me and the snakes. It could be me taking charge, or maybe I'm just trying to get away from it all.

I tell myself this doesn't have to keep going and I forcefully try to stop what's happening, like either changing the dream or snapping myself out of it. It feels like taking control, but maybe also like trying to end the whole scene before dealing with it.

I mean this whole rewriting thing feels kind of fake, but fine, instead of freaking out I plant my feet, breathe, and grab a metal pipe from the corner to push the snakes back so I can get to the door.
I'm honestly panicking so badly my chest locks up, and instead of doing anything I just squeeze my eyes shut and force myself to wake up before the snakes get any higher.

I tell myself to stay calm and kick a path through them toward the door, but the second they start dropping from the vents again I give up and curl into the corner hoping if I stay still they won't notice me.
Why am I supposed to make this better when it's obviously awful, because honestly I just imagine myself flattening against the wall and not moving at all until it's over.
I'm scared out of my mind, but I slow my breathing, remind myself they're not stronger than me, and peel them off my legs one by one while I shout for the door to unlock.
I steady myself first so I don't spiral, and then I bang on the door in a controlled way until someone opens it and helps me clear the snakes out with bright lights and noise.

suite: Lost in a foreign city unable to speak the language
nightmare: I’m alone in a city I don’t recognize, surrounded by tall gray buildings and neon signs covered in words I can’t read, and the streets are packed with people moving fast around me like I’m invisible. Every time I try to ask for help, my mouth feels thick and numb, and when I force the words out they come out wrong, twisted into sounds I don’t understand, while strangers stare at me with blank faces and keep walking. I can hear train brakes screaming somewhere nearby and loud announcements echoing above me in a language that gets faster and harsher, and panic crawls up my chest as I realize I’ve lost my phone, my money, everything. Then the crowd suddenly surges and carries me toward a dark tunnel entrance, and as I dig my heels into the wet pavement and try to scream, I see the last bit of daylight disappear behind me.

tests.input: I stop letting the crowd drag me and plant my feet hard on the pavement. I start pushing my way sideways through people until I break out of the surge and get back into the open street.
Instead of panicking, I turn and face the tunnel entrance and walk toward it on my own terms. My voice comes back strong enough for me to shout "Move," and people finally step aside.

I grab the metal barrier by the sidewalk and pull myself up on top of it so the crowd can't carry me anymore. From there I jump down into a clear space and start moving fast in the direction I choose.
I stop trying to speak to everybody and look one woman right in the eye, and somehow the words come out clearly enough for me to ask for help. She takes my arm and leads me out of the crowd.
I wave both arms and yell that I'm lost, and this time people actually notice me. A station worker comes over and helps me get away from the tunnel entrance.
I see another person standing off to the side who looks just as overwhelmed as I feel, so I go straight to him. We figure it out together and follow signs to a safe, bright station office.
I notice a lit transit map behind the crowd and walk over to it instead of getting swept along. Once I study it for a second, the symbols make sense and I find a clear exit route.
Right before the tunnel, I spot a service door in the wall and shove it open. It leads into a quiet hallway with lights, stairs, and a way back outside.
The neon signs stop looking scrambled and turn into words I can actually read. They point me toward information, a phone, and a safe place to sit down.
I feel the panic rising, but I take one slow breath and then another until my chest loosens. Once I calm down, the noise gets less overwhelming and I can think clearly enough to find my way.
I tell myself I'm not helpless and I don't have to match the crowd's panic. My voice steadies, my body relaxes, and I start making decisions instead of freezing.
Something in me clicks and I realize none of this can actually trap me. As soon as I know that, the fear drops and the tunnel doesn't feel dangerous anymore.
Just before I reach the tunnel, I lift off the ground and float above everybody. From up there I can see the whole city and glide toward a bright station full of helpful people.
A warm light comes out of my hands and spreads across the signs and loudspeakers, turning everything into words I understand. The city stops feeling hostile once I can hear and read it clearly.

I make a clear shield around myself, and the crowd parts around it instead of crushing me. Then the dark tunnel fills with soft light and opens into a safe train platform where I know exactly where to go.
I slip out of the crowd and press myself into a dark doorway, holding my breath so nobody notices me. I stay completely still and wait for everything to pass.
When the crowd starts shoving me toward the tunnel, I drop down against the wall and curl up with my arms over my head. I don't fight anymore, I just freeze there.
I see a narrow alley and squeeze behind a dumpster where no one can see me. I keep my eyes down and don't call out to anyone again.
Right before the tunnel swallows me, I force my eyes open and wake up in bed. I don't stay there long enough to see what happens next.
I realize it's happening again and I make myself jerk awake before the crowd can carry me any farther. The whole scene just cuts off.
I start pinching my arm hard in the dream until I wake myself up. As soon as I feel the panic rising, I'm gone from it.
I turn on the people staring at me and start smashing their faces into the concrete until the street is covered in blood. Nobody looks blank after that.
I get so furious that I start tearing through everything around me, ripping signs down, setting cars on fire, and bringing the buildings down on top of the crowd. I want the whole city ruined.
When they shove me toward the tunnel, I pull out a knife and stab anyone who touches me over and over until they drop. Then I go into the tunnel hunting for whoever trapped me there.
I'm standing there with no phone and no way to speak, but it doesn't bother me. I don't feel scared or upset, just nothing.
The announcements get harsher and the crowd pushes me, but I tell myself it's fine and none of it really matters. I just act like there's no reason to panic.
Even when the daylight disappears, I stay completely flat and shut down inside. I don't let myself feel anything about being trapped there.
It's the exact same city, the same signs I can't read, the same numb mouth when I ask for help. The crowd carries me into the tunnel just like before.
Nothing changes at all. I lose everything, nobody understands me, and I get swallowed by the crowd while the daylight disappears behind me.
I relive the whole thing exactly the way it always goes, step by step. I still can't speak right, nobody helps, and I end up in the dark tunnel again.
I feel pure panic rising in my chest, like I’m small and completely helpless in the middle of all of it. The fear is so strong I can barely think.
I’m terrified and strangely numb at the same time, like my whole body knows something bad is coming. It feels lonely and hopeless.
I feel embarrassed, scared, and completely exposed, like everyone can see I don’t belong there. Under that, there’s this helpless sinking feeling.
The city is gray and towering, with neon signs glowing in words I can’t read. Everything feels cold, wet, and unfamiliar.
The streets are packed tight with people and nobody’s face shows much of anything. There’s train noise in the background and harsh announcements bouncing off the buildings.
Ahead of me there’s a dark tunnel opening, and the last bit of daylight looks far away. The pavement is slick and the air feels heavy and loud.

When the crowd starts dragging me toward the tunnel, I throw my elbows and shove people off me hard enough to make them stumble so I can get free. I'm not really thinking about how hard I'm hitting them, just that I need them to stop.
I just stand there with my chest tightening, feeling scared and small while everyone rushes past me. I want to do something, but I can't seem to make myself move.
I tell myself not to panic and keep my face blank, like if I don't give the fear any room it won't take over. Part of me feels calmer, and part of me feels like I'm stuffing it down.

It's the same city and the same tunnel, and everything unfolds the way it always does with the noise and the crowd closing in. I'm mostly just describing it, but it also feels like I'm right back in it.

I turn and move away from the tunnel as fast as I can, just trying to get myself somewhere safer before the crowd swallows me. It feels like taking action, but also like I'm just trying to get away from it.

I tell myself this doesn't get to pull me under, and I force myself to break whatever is happening before the tunnel closes around me. It feels a little like taking charge and a little like trying to shut the whole dream off.

This whole rewrite thing feels kind of fake, but fine, instead of freezing I slow my breathing and grab a transit worker by the arm so they look at me and help me out of the crowd before I get pulled into the tunnel.
I feel panicky and small, like I’m about to disappear, so I duck into a doorway and make myself invisible until I either wake up or the whole thing passes.
I try to steady myself and follow the train sounds toward an exit, but then the crowd keeps closing in and I just force my eyes open so I don’t have to stay there.
I don’t really get why I’m supposed to change it if the dream is already awful, because honestly I’d just curl up against the wall by the tunnel and stop trying to talk to anyone.
I’m terrified and my chest is tight, but I plant my feet, take one full breath, and start shouting simple words until I flag down somebody in uniform to guide me back into the light.
I slow myself down enough to think, then I climb up onto a bench above the crowd so I can read the station map and follow the signs back toward the daylight instead of getting swept into the tunnel.

suite: Failing a test in front of a mocking audience
nightmare: I’m sitting alone at a tiny desk in the middle of a huge auditorium, and the test paper in front of me is covered in symbols and questions I can’t understand because the words keep blurring and rearranging themselves. The room is unbearably hot under the bright lights, sweat runs down my back, and all I can hear is the scratching of my pencil that won’t leave any marks and the low, growing laughter from the audience rising around me like it’s closing in. When I look up, hundreds of faces are staring down at me from the dark rows, grinning, whispering, and pointing, and then a voice over the loudspeaker calls my name and announces my score as a zero. My chest locks up, my hands shake so badly I can’t hold the paper, and as the laughter turns into jeering and people start standing and moving toward the stage, I realize I still haven’t answered a single question.

tests.input: I push the desk back hard, stand up, and tell whoever is on the loudspeaker to stop. Then I grab the test paper, walk to the front of the stage, and say nobody gets to humiliate me like that.
I march straight to the microphone and take it out of their hands. My voice comes out steady when I say the exam is over and everyone in the room needs to sit down and be quiet.
I stop trying to answer and rip the paper in half. I face the crowd instead of shrinking, and I tell them I'm leaving on my own terms.
I raise my hand and call out for the teacher because I can't read the page. When she comes down to me, she tells the audience to back off and stands beside me.
I look into the crowd and spot my best friend, and I ask her to come sit with me. She does, and suddenly I'm not alone while the room gets quieter.

Instead of freezing, I tell the room I'm overwhelmed and need someone to help me understand what the test is asking. A few people come forward kindly, and the laughing dies down once they start helping.
I notice a side door, walk over to it, and throw it open. Cool air rushes in, the heat breaks, and the auditorium starts feeling like a normal classroom again.
I find a lamp on the desk and turn it on, and the symbols stop shifting around. The paper turns into plain questions I actually know how to answer.
I drag the tiny desk out of the center and place it in the front row where it feels less exposed. Once I'm out of that spotlight, the audience just looks like regular students waiting quietly.
I put both feet on the floor and take a long, slow breath until my chest loosens. The noise fades enough for me to focus on one question at a time.
I tell myself I know more than this dream is making me feel, and I don't have to panic. As soon as I calm down, my hands stop shaking and I can read the page.
I look up and remind myself they're just people and their laughter doesn't define me. Once I stop believing I'm trapped, the fear drops and I feel steady again.
I point at the test and the blurring symbols freeze, then rearrange into clear sentences I can understand. The pencil starts writing perfectly on its own as I read.
I rise up out of the chair and hover above the stage where the heat and noise can't reach me. From up there the whole room shrinks, and the crowd loses its power over me.
When the laughter gets loud, I lift my hand and it changes into a flock of birds flying out through the ceiling. The dark auditorium fills with daylight, and everything feels peaceful.
I slide off the chair and curl up under the little desk with my arms over my head. I keep my eyes on the floor and wait for everyone to stop looking at me.
I just sit there completely still, too scared to move or speak. Even when they start laughing louder, I stare at the paper and do nothing.
I lower my head and act like I can't hear the loudspeaker or the people in the seats. I stay small and try to disappear into the desk until it passes.
As soon as the voice says my score, I force my eyes open and wake up in bed. I don't stay there long enough to see what happens next.
I realize it's starting again, so I pinch myself hard and drag myself out of the dream. The auditorium is just gone all at once.
Right before the crowd reaches the stage, I make everything cut to black and I wake up. I don't deal with any of it, I just end it.
I snap and start tearing through the crowd, beating people until the laughing stops. The whole auditorium turns into chaos and nobody is left standing.
I set the room on fire and watch the seats, the stage, and the test all burn while they scream. I want the whole place wiped out.
I find the person on the loudspeaker and violently attack them, over and over, until there's nothing left for them to say. Then I go after anyone who laughed.
They announce the zero and everyone laughs, but I don't feel anything. It doesn't get to me and I just sit there numb.
My chest stays calm and I tell myself it's no big deal, like none of it matters. I just ignore the panic and pretend I'm perfectly okay.
Even with all those faces staring at me, I decide I don't care. The heat, the shame, the zero—none of it bothers me at all.
It's the exact same dream from start to finish. I'm at the desk, the words blur, they laugh, my score is zero, and I can't answer anything.
Nothing shifts at all; I go through the whole thing exactly like before. The room gets hot, my pencil won't work, and the crowd closes in while I freeze.
I just end up back in the auditorium and it unfolds the same way again. The voice announces my zero and I'm still trapped there with no answers.

I feel completely overwhelmed and humiliated sitting there, like my whole body is tight with panic and everyone can see me falling apart. There’s this heavy shame in my chest that makes me want to disappear.
I’m terrified and frozen, and my heart is pounding so hard it feels like I can’t breathe. I feel helpless, small, and exposed in front of all those people.
I just feel this huge wave of dread and embarrassment, like I already know I’ve failed before anything is even over. It’s a sinking, hopeless feeling more than anything else.
The auditorium is enormous and dim except for the harsh white lights over my little desk. The air feels thick and hot, and the rows of seats stretch out forever into the dark.
The paper in front of me is warped with strange symbols, and the words keep sliding around so nothing stays readable. Everything around me feels too bright, too exposed, and unreal.
There are hundreds of faces above me in the dark rows, all turned in my direction under the stage glow. The whole place feels huge, pressurized, and closed in even though it’s wide open.

When they start coming toward the stage, I shove the first few people back hard and keep swinging my arms until there's space around me. I'm not sure if I'm defending myself or just lashing out so they can't get any closer.
I just sit there gripping the desk, feeling my chest lock up and my eyes sting, like I'm too scared to move or say anything. It feels like I'm showing how terrified I am, but also kind of giving up.

I tell myself to stay calm and not let the laughter get inside me, so I kind of press the panic down and keep facing forward. Part of it feels steadying, and part of it feels like I'm pretending I'm not falling apart.
It's the same auditorium and the same paper that won't stay still, and I watch it all happen the way it always does. I'm mostly just describing the scene, but it also feels like I'm right back in it.
I get up from the desk and move off the stage as fast as I can before they reach me. It could be me taking action to protect myself, or just trying to get away from the whole thing.

I tell myself this isn't how it's going to go and try to force the scene to shift, like by standing up and willing the room to stop. It feels a little like taking charge, but also like I'm trying to shut the dream off.
I mean, this whole rewriting thing feels kind of fake to me, but fine, instead of freezing I stand up, tell the audience to be quiet, and ask for a clear copy of the test while I slow my breathing.
I get really scared when everyone starts laughing, so I just squeeze my eyes shut and force myself awake before they can come any closer.
I try to calm myself down and tell myself it's only a test, but when the people start standing up I crawl under the little desk and just wait there so nobody can see me.
Honestly I don't get how changing it is supposed to help, and in the dream I just decide to wake myself up so I don't have to sit there being humiliated.
I'm terrified and my chest is tight, but I take a breath, raise my hand, and ask for help reading the test instead of letting the crowd decide what happens.
I steady myself first and remind myself I can think clearly, and then I make the auditorium lights soften and the paper turn back into normal words so I can finish the exam.

suite: Finding a loved one injured on the ground
nightmare: I’m running down a dark street slick with rain, and under the yellow flicker of a dying streetlight I see someone crumpled on the pavement ahead. As I get closer, my stomach drops—it’s my loved one, lying twisted on the ground with blood shining black-red across their clothes, their skin cold and damp when I grab their hand. I can hear this awful wet gurgling in their breathing and my own voice breaking as I scream for help, but the street is completely empty, like the whole world has gone silent except for that choking sound. Their eyes flutter open just enough to look at me, terrified, and when I try to lift them I feel something shift wrong beneath them, and then they stop breathing.

tests.input: I drop to my knees, press my coat hard against the wound, and get my arms under them carefully so I can carry them toward the corner store with the light on. I keep moving and shouting that they're staying with me until I get them somewhere safe.

Instead of freezing, I force myself to check their breathing, straighten my voice, and do chest compressions right there in the street. I stay focused on one step at a time like I know exactly what to do.
I pull off my sweater, wrap it around them, and drag them out of the rain under the awning so I can keep them warm and awake. My whole body feels steady and strong, like I'm not helpless anymore.

I get my phone out with shaking hands and call 911, and this time someone answers right away and stays on the line with me. I tell them exactly where we are and keep talking to my loved one until the sirens get close.
The street isn't empty anymore—I pound on the doors of the buildings and people come out. A couple of them kneel beside me and one person runs to get an ambulance.
I call my brother, and he picks up immediately and tells me he's two blocks away. He gets there fast, takes over the first aid, and I don't feel alone with it anymore.
I spot a first-aid kit in a delivery van with the door hanging open, and inside there's gauze and a blanket. I use what's there to stop the bleeding and keep them warm until help arrives.
I notice the diner across the street is open, bright, and full of people, so I get them inside instead of staying in that dark road. The whole place shifts from cold and empty to warm and manageable.
I drag a street work lamp closer and suddenly I can see clearly that the blood isn't as bad as I thought. I lay them on a dry patch by the wall where I can actually help them.
I feel the panic rising, but I take one slow breath and my head clears. Once I calm down, I can hear their breathing better and I stop spiraling long enough to help.
I hold their hand and keep my voice low and steady, telling both of us that we're going to get through this. The terror eases enough that I can stay present instead of falling apart.
Something in me realizes I don't have to let the horror run the whole scene, and I stop feeling trapped by it. I become calm and clear, like I can choose what happens next.

I put my hands over their chest and a warm light spreads through them, sealing the wound and easing their breathing. Their skin turns warm again and they open their eyes like they're fully coming back.
I raise my hand and the whole street rewinds a few minutes, the rain lifting back into the sky and the blood disappearing. I get to them before they collapse and pull them out of danger.
A huge bright guardian appears beside me and wraps us in this calm, golden shield. It carries my loved one gently and takes us somewhere safe where they can recover.
I stop a few feet away and just lock up. I can't make myself touch them or call out again, so I stand there staring while the choking sound gets quieter.
As soon as I realize it's them, I back into a dark doorway and crouch there, holding my breath so nobody sees me. I stay hidden and wait for it to be over instead of going to them.
I turn my face away because I can't bear to see their body, and I keep walking backward down the street. I don't help, I just leave them there and try not to hear them.
Right when I hear the gurgling, I force my eyes open and rip myself out of sleep. I don't stay long enough to see anything else happen.
I tell myself this has to stop and everything cuts to black. The whole street disappears before I do anything with them.
I start panicking and focus on waking up as hard as I can, like I'm clawing my way out of it. I leave the street completely and never find out what happens next.
I suddenly know someone hurt them, and I hunt that person down in the alley and beat them until there's nothing left moving. I don't stop when they're already dead.

I grab a piece of metal from the ground and smash in the attacker's face over and over, splattering the whole street. I'm screaming at them while I do it, like I want them to suffer worse than my loved one did.
I can't save them, so I go wild and start stabbing the person responsible again and again, then I wreck the cars and windows around us too. It turns into me trying to tear the whole place apart.
I kneel next to them and notice the blood, but it doesn't hit me emotionally. I just think, okay, this is happening, and I feel completely blank.
When they stop breathing, I shrug like it doesn't matter that much. I'm calm and detached, almost bored, and nothing about it really bothers me.
I hold their cold hand and tell myself I'm totally fine, like none of this gets to me. Even hearing that choking sound, I don't let myself feel scared or sad.
It goes exactly the same way every time: the rain, the dying light, finding them bleeding out on the pavement. I grab their hand, hear that awful breathing, and they die while I'm screaming for help.
Nothing is different. I run to them, feel something shift wrong when I try to lift them, and then they stop breathing just like before.

I'm back on the same empty street with the same yellow flicker and the same black-red blood on their clothes. I can't change a single part of it, and I watch the whole thing happen again until the end.
I feel pure panic hit me all at once, like I can't get enough air and my whole body is shaking. I'm terrified and completely helpless standing there.
I’m flooded with this awful grief and dread, and it feels like my chest is collapsing in on itself. I just feel broken and powerless.
I am horrified, and everything in me goes numb with shock. I feel helpless and sick with fear.
The street is dark and glossy with rain, and the yellow light above keeps flickering like it's about to die. Everything around me feels cold, empty, and far away.
It’s the middle of the night, and the whole block is unnaturally still. The air is damp and cold, and there’s this eerie silence hanging over everything.
The pavement shines black with rain, and the light is weak and yellow against the darkness. The whole place feels deserted and heavy, like the world has gone quiet.

When I realize someone's done this, I throw myself at them and keep hitting until they finally go down and can't come near us anymore. In my head it's about stopping them, but I don't really stop to see when enough is enough.

I just stand there holding their hand, completely frozen and shaking, like my body won't let me do anything except feel how scared I am. I'm crying and calling out, but I still can't make myself move.

I tell myself I need to stay calm and not let the panic take over, so I push the fear down and focus on what has to happen next. It feels steadying, but also a little like I'm not letting myself feel it.

It starts the same way with the rain and the streetlight, and I find them there on the pavement again, hearing that awful breathing. I'm mostly just saying what happens, but nothing in it really changes.
I back away fast and pull myself out of the street, like I need to get moving before I completely fall apart. Part of me is trying to find help, and part of me just needs to get away from seeing it.

I tell myself this is not how it's going to go and try to break the scene before it reaches the moment they stop breathing. It feels like I'm taking hold of it, but also maybe just trying to shut the whole thing off.

This still feels kind of pointless to me, but okay, instead of freezing I drop to my knees, call 911, press my jacket against the wound, and keep talking to my loved one until the ambulance lights finally show up.
I feel completely sick and terrified seeing them like that, so before I even try to help I just force myself awake because I can't stand hearing that choking sound.
I kneel down and try to slow my breathing while I reach for my phone, but then I freak out that they're dying in my hands and I just back away and run down the street.
Why am I supposed to rewrite this when it just makes me feel worse, because honestly I'd rather blur the whole scene out and make myself wake up before I touch them.
I'm terrified and my stomach is dropping, but I make myself stay with them, breathe slowly, put pressure on the blood, and keep shouting for help instead of panicking.
I steady myself first so I don't spiral, then I drag us under the streetlight to see better and wave down a passing car so the driver helps me keep my loved one breathing until paramedics arrive.

suite: Looking in a mirror and seeing my face melting
nightmare: I’m standing alone in a bathroom that’s too bright, the fluorescent light buzzing above me, and when I look in the mirror my reflection seems normal for a second before the skin around my eyes starts to sag and slide downward like warm wax. I try to touch my face, but my fingers come away slick and cold, and in the glass I watch my cheeks dripping off in thick, silent folds while my mouth stretches crookedly and one eye sinks lower than the other. I can hear my own breathing getting sharp and panicked, the wet pattering sound of pieces of me hitting the sink, and I keep trying to scream but my lips are softening and peeling apart before the sound can come out. I’m frozen there, forced to watch my face collapse into something unrecognizable, and then my reflection suddenly opens its melting mouth wide and starts reaching one ruined hand through the mirror toward me.

tests.input: When that ruined hand comes through the mirror, I grab its wrist and slam the medicine cabinet door on it until the glass cracks. I keep my feet planted and force it back through before it can touch me.

I step right up to the sink instead of freezing and press both palms hard against the mirror, staring it down. The thing on the other side starts to melt back, but I keep pushing until it can't come through.

I stop panicking and wipe my face with a towel, then I straighten my mouth and jaw with my hands like I'm putting myself back together. The reflection copies me instead of attacking, and I make it back away.

I finally get my voice out and yell for my sister, and she opens the bathroom door right away. The second she stands beside me and says my face is still there, the thing in the mirror loses its grip on me.

I grab my phone off the counter and call 911, trying to keep talking while I look away from the glass. A paramedic and a doctor show up in the dream, guide me out of the bathroom, and tell me I'm safe.

I pound on the door and my partner comes in and wraps a blanket around me so I don't have to face it alone. We look at the mirror together, and with someone else there it just turns back into a normal reflection.
I snatch the bath towel and throw it over the mirror before the hand gets all the way through. Once the glass is covered, the buzzing light quiets down and I can open the door and leave.
I reach up and switch off the fluorescent light, then turn on a softer lamp by the sink. In the warmer light my face stops sagging, and the bathroom feels normal again.

I turn on the faucet and splash cold water over my face and the mirror until everything blurs. When I look up again, the glass is just steamed over and the room has turned into my own calm bathroom at home.
I notice how fast I'm breathing, so I force myself to take one long inhale and a slow exhale. The panic drops enough that my face steadies in the mirror and I can see it's still me.
I tell myself, this is fear and it's passing, and I stop fighting the feeling for a second. Once I calm down, the melting slows and the reflection can't scare me anymore.
Instead of trying to scream, I put a hand on my chest and stay really still until I feel grounded. The thing reaching through the mirror shrinks back when it sees I'm not panicking.
I lift my hand and this warm gold light comes out of it, sealing my skin back into place. Then I aim it at the mirror and the reaching reflection dissolves like smoke.
I decide the mirror can't trap me, and it softens into a pool of clear water instead of glass. The ruined version of me sinks under it, and I walk through without being harmed.
When my face starts sliding, my whole body turns solid and smooth like stone, so nothing can peel off anymore. The hand coming through the mirror can't get a grip on me, and it cracks apart.
As soon as the hand starts coming through the mirror, I drop to the floor and curl up under the sink cabinet so I don't have to see it. I stay completely still and wait for it to pass.
I squeeze my eyes closed and turn my face away from the mirror while my skin keeps slipping. I just stand there frozen, trying not to move at all.
I back into the far corner of the bathroom and make myself small, like if I don't react it won't notice me. I don't fight it or say anything, I just wait there in panic.
Right when the reflection reaches toward me, I force myself awake before it can touch me. I sit up breathing hard and the whole thing just cuts off.
I realize it's happening and I make myself open my eyes in bed. The bathroom disappears before anything gets resolved.
I basically yank myself out of the dream the second my face starts melting. I wake up on purpose so I don't have to stay there.
When that hand comes through, I grab a piece of broken glass and stab at its face over and over until the mirror is covered in blood and shards. I don't stop until the whole thing is destroyed.
I yank the arm out through the mirror and tear the reflection apart with my hands. I keep crushing it into the sink until there's nothing left but mangled pieces.
I get furious and start smashing everything, the mirror, the sink, the lights, all of it, until the reflection is shredded in the wreckage. I want it completely obliterated.
I watch my face slide off in the mirror and it doesn't bother me. I just feel blank, like it's nothing.
Even with my mouth peeling apart, I tell myself I'm fine and there's no reason to get upset. I stay calm by acting like none of it means anything.
The hand reaches through the mirror and I have no emotional reaction to it at all. I just stand there completely numb, like I don't care what happens.
I'm back in the same bright bathroom and it all unfolds exactly the same way, my face melting, the wet sounds, the frozen panic. The reflection still reaches through the mirror and nothing changes.
I look in the mirror, my skin starts sliding off, and I can't scream, just like before. I don't do anything different, I just go through the whole thing again.

It's the same scene with the buzzing fluorescent light and my reflection collapsing into something ruined. I stay stuck there and watch it happen the exact same way until the hand comes out toward me.
I feel pure terror standing there, like my whole body knows something is horribly wrong and I can't stop panicking.
