suite: Trying to run through thick mud while being chased
nightmare: I’m running through a field of thick, black mud that sucks at my legs like hands, and every step takes everything I have just to move a few inches. I can hear something behind me crashing closer through the wet ground—heavy, uneven footsteps and this ragged breathing that doesn’t sound human—and when I try to look back, my neck feels stiff and my chest locks up with panic. The mud is ice-cold and crawling over my shoes, pulling me down harder and harder, and I can smell this rotten swamp smell while my heart pounds so loud it drowns out my own screams. Just as my foot comes completely free and I lurch forward, something grabs my ankle from behind and yanks me backward into the mud.

tests.input: When something grabs my ankle, I whirl around instead of freezing and slam my heel down into the mud until its grip loosens. I yank my leg free and plant myself solidly, facing whatever is behind me.
I stop fighting the mud long enough to square my shoulders and turn toward the breathing. I tell it, "You're not dragging me anywhere," and I push back hard against the thing holding me.

I drop low, dig my hands into the ground, and drag myself forward with all my strength instead of panicking. Once my foot comes loose, I get up and run in a straight line like I'm finally in control of my body.
I shout for my brother, and he comes running across the field with a rope. He throws it to me and keeps talking to me until I can pull myself out of the mud.
This time when I scream, people actually hear me from a road nearby and come toward the sound. They reach down, grab my arms, and help me stand while the thing behind me stops coming closer.
I stop trying to handle it alone and yell, "I need help right now." Someone appears beside me, steady and calm, and helps me get my footing so I can move again.
I see a thick branch half-buried in the mud and grab it like a walking stick. Using it to brace myself, I lever my legs free and make it onto a patch of dry ground.
The black mud starts to firm up under my feet until it turns into a narrow trail. I follow that solid path out of the field while the crashing sound fades farther behind me.
I notice an old fence post sticking out and pull myself toward it. Once I grab it, I climb over into a dry pasture and the swamp smell disappears.
I feel my chest locking up, so I force myself to take one slow breath and then another. As I calm down, the panic stops running the dream and I can think clearly enough to get unstuck.
I tell myself that the fear is huge, but it can't actually control me. Once I say that, my body loosens, my neck turns normally, and I stop feeling so helpless.
Instead of spiraling, I steady myself and focus on one step at a time. The more confident I feel, the less the mud pulls at me, like it loses power when I stop feeding it fear.
Right before I get dragged under, my body rises off the ground and I float above the mud. I watch the thing below me shrink as I drift out of reach.
I turn around and a bright light comes out of my hands, flooding the whole field. Whatever was chasing me can't come near it, and the mud dries up where the light touches.
When it grabs my ankle, I change into a huge animal with strong legs and tear free easily. I bound across the swamp in a few leaps and leave the whole thing behind me.
When I hear it getting close, I stop fighting the mud and let myself go limp. I lie face down and pretend I'm dead so maybe it will pass over me.
I drag myself off to the side where the mud is deeper and sink down behind a patch of tall swamp grass. I keep completely still and don't look back, just trying not to be noticed.
My body just locks up and I stop moving altogether. I stand there in the mud with my eyes shut, hoping if I don't do anything it won't find me.
Right when it grabs my ankle, I force my eyes open and rip myself out of sleep. I don't stay there long enough to see what it is.
As soon as the panic hits my chest, I tell myself to wake up and everything cuts out. The field and the mud just disappear before anything else happens.
I feel the breathing right behind me and I start thrashing until I wake myself up. The only way out is ending the dream completely.
I spin around with a machete and start chopping at whatever grabbed me until it's in pieces in the mud. I keep swinging long after it stops moving.
I wrench my leg free, tackle it, and slam its head into the swamp over and over. I don't stop until the water is black and still and I know I've crushed it.
I set the field on fire and let the flames swallow the thing chasing me, the mud, all of it. I watch everything burn down because I want nothing left standing.
It grabs my ankle and pulls me under, but I don't feel scared or upset at all. It's just happening and I don't care.
The mud is freezing and that breathing is right behind me, and I'm completely unbothered by it. I just tell myself it's nothing and keep my face blank.
Even when my chest tightens and I hear myself screaming, inside I feel flat. None of it gets to me and I have no reaction to it.
It plays out exactly the same way every time. I run through the black mud, hear it coming, and it grabs my ankle and drags me back under.
I can't make anything different happen. The field, the smell, the panic, the thing behind me—it's all the same and I get pulled down into the mud again.
I just go through the whole nightmare as it is, from struggling for each step to getting yanked backward by my ankle. There isn't any change or escape in it.
I feel pure panic in my chest, like I can't breathe and I'm completely trapped. I'm terrified and helpless.
I am so scared I can barely think, and this heavy dread just takes over my whole body. It feels like hopelessness more than anything.
I feel small, weak, and overwhelmed, like the fear is bigger than me. There's this awful sense that I'm not going to get away.
The whole field is thick with black mud, and the air smells rotten like a swamp. Everything feels icy and heavy around me.
It's dim and gray, and the ground looks endless and wet in every direction. The place feels dead and suffocatingly still.
Behind me there are heavy, uneven sounds in the mud and this ragged breathing that doesn't sound human. The whole scene feels cold, foul, and wrong.
When whatever grabs my ankle pulls me down, I kick and slam at it with all I've got until it lets go, and I don't really stop until it's gone still enough for me to get free.
I just go rigid in the mud and feel the panic take over, like I can't make my body do anything except stand there and feel how scared I am.
I tell myself not to freak out and keep moving, like if I press the fear down enough it won't get in the way.
It all plays out in that same black mud with the crashing steps behind me, basically the way it always does, and I just watch it happening again.
I wrench my leg loose and haul myself forward as fast as I can, just trying to get out of that part of the swamp before it reaches me.
I sort of tell myself this isn't how it's going to go and force everything in me to make the scene stop or shift somehow.

This whole rewrite thing feels kind of fake to me, but if I go with it then I stop fighting the panic, yell for help, and imagine a bright rescue light pulling me out of the mud while I turn and face whatever's behind me.
I'm so panicked when that hand grabs my ankle that I can't even think straight, and I just jolt myself awake before I have to see what it is.
I try to slow my breathing and yank my leg free like I'm going to deal with it, but then I freak out again and decide to bury myself in the mud so it can't see me.
I honestly don't get how changing a dream is supposed to help anything, so in the rewrite I just crawl into the thick mud and stay completely still so whatever's chasing me passes by.
I'm terrified and my chest is locking up, but I make myself take one full breath, plant my feet on solid ground, and turn around to face the thing instead of letting it drag me under.
I steady myself first and let the panic come down, and then I imagine the mud drying into firm ground under me so I can move freely and confront whatever is chasing me.

suite: Trying to lock a door against an intruder but the lock is broken
nightmare: I’m in my house at night, and everything is wrong—too quiet except for the slow, heavy footsteps coming down the hallway toward me. My hands are slick with sweat as I shove the door closed and fumble with the lock, but it just spins uselessly under my fingers, clicking without catching, while the knob on the other side gives a soft, deliberate rattle. I can hear my own breathing turning ragged, feel the wood trembling against my palms, and see the shadow of someone standing just outside, blotting out the strip of light under the door. Then the rattling stops completely, and in the silence I feel the knob begin to turn, slowly, from the other side.

tests.input: I stop backing up, unlock the door myself, and pull it open before they can. I stand there looking straight at whoever is outside and tell them they need to leave my house now.
When the knob starts turning, I plant my feet and push hard against the door until it swings back on them. I rush forward and force the person into the hallway so they can't trap me anymore.
Instead of freezing, I square my shoulders and walk toward the door on purpose. The fear is still there, but I take control of the room and make it clear I'm not helpless.
I yell for my brother from the next room, and he answers right away. Hearing him come down the hall makes me feel less alone, and the person outside backs off.
My hands are shaking, but I grab my phone and call 911 while I keep talking loudly through the door. The dispatcher stays with me until I hear help pulling up outside.
I start shouting for help out the window, and the neighbors switch on their lights and come outside. As soon as other people are there, the hallway doesn't feel dangerous anymore.
I drag a dresser and a chair in front of the door and wedge them tight under the knob. The door stops shaking, and I finally feel like I have something solid between me and whatever's out there.
I notice the bedroom window is open, so I climb out onto the porch roof and get down safely. Once I'm outside in the fresh air, the house doesn't have that trapped feeling anymore.

When I switch on the light, the shadow under the door shrinks and I realize it's just my coat hanging near a fan, making strange sounds. The whole house goes back to normal and quiet in a peaceful way.
I make myself take one slow breath and then another until my chest loosens. Once I calm down, the rattling at the door doesn't control me the same way.
I suddenly know I'm safe in my own room, and that certainty settles through my body. The panic drains off, and I can think clearly instead of just reacting.
I recognize that this is a dream, and as soon as I know that, the fear drops way down. I stand there calmly and the door loses all its power over me.
I lift my hand and the lock glows, sealing the door shut with a kind of blue light. The person outside can't touch it anymore, and I feel completely protected.
My body suddenly fills with this huge calm strength, and I grow taller than the hallway itself. Whoever is outside feels tiny, and they can't threaten me anymore.
I snap my fingers and warm light rushes through the house, washing every room clean. The shadow under the door disappears, and the whole place feels protected like nothing bad can enter.
I back away from the door and crawl into the closet, pulling the coats over me so whoever is outside won't see me. I stay completely still and hold my breath while the handle keeps moving.
I slide down to the floor beside the bed and just freeze there. I don't call out or try anything, I just make myself small and wait for it to pass.
I stand silently behind the door with my hands over my mouth, pretending the house is empty. Even when the knob starts turning, I don't move.
As soon as the knob starts to turn, I force my eyes open and drag myself out of the dream. I wake up before I ever see who's there.
I tell myself this has to stop right now, and everything just cuts out. I'm suddenly awake in bed with my heart pounding.
Right when the shadow fills the doorway, I jerk myself awake on purpose. I don't stay long enough for anything else to happen.
When the door opens, I grab a knife and lunge at the person, stabbing them over and over until they drop. I keep going long after they're not moving because I want to make sure they're ruined.
I swing the lamp into their face, then I keep smashing them with it until there's blood all over the hallway. I don't stop until their body is unrecognizable.
I decide if someone's coming for me, then nobody gets out, so I set the room on fire and trap them inside with me. I watch everything burn just to destroy them completely.
The footsteps come closer and the knob turns, but I don't feel scared or anything really. It's like none of it matters to me.
I just stand there and tell myself I'm fine, completely fine. Whoever is outside the door doesn't bother me.
I hear the rattling and see the shadow, and I basically shrug because I don't care. My chest isn't tight anymore because I shut all of that off.
It's the exact same house, same footsteps, same broken lock under my hand. The shadow stops outside the door and the knob slowly turns, just like always.
Nothing changes at all—I still shove the door, the lock still won't catch, and I can hear myself breathing hard. Then the rattling stops and I know the person is about to come in.
I go through the whole thing exactly the same way again. I'm at the door with my sweaty hands, the light disappears under it, and the handle starts turning from the other side.
I feel terrified, like my whole body is frozen and I can't make myself do anything. There's this helpless panic in my chest that just keeps building.
I'm so scared I feel weak and shaky, like all the strength drains out of me. It feels hopeless and I just wait there in pure dread.
I am completely panicked and numb at the same time. It feels like fear has me pinned in place.
The house is dark and unnaturally still, with the hallway stretching out in shadow. The air feels cold and heavy.
It's nighttime in my room, and the only light is a thin strip under the door. Everything around me feels dim, cramped, and too quiet.
The whole house has this tense, suffocating feeling, like the silence is pressing in on me. The door and walls seem close around me, and the hallway outside is black.

When the door starts opening, I grab the nearest heavy thing and swing at him over and over until he goes down and the hallway finally gets quiet. It feels like I'm protecting myself, but I also don't really stop once I've started.
I just stand there with my hands on the door, shaking and trying not to fall apart, because I'm too scared to do anything else. It feels like all I can do is stay there and feel how terrified I am.
I tell myself to stay calm and not let the fear take over, so I kind of shove it to the side and keep going. I'm in control, but I'm also not really letting myself feel much of it.

It plays out the same way, with the footsteps, the lock slipping, and the shadow under the door while I wait for the knob to turn. I'm mostly just describing it, but it also feels like I'm right back inside it.

As soon as I realize the lock won't hold, I move away from the door and get out of there as fast as I can. It feels like taking action, but mostly what I'm doing is escaping before I have to face him.

I tell myself this isn't going to happen and force myself to break out of it somehow, like either taking control or just making the whole thing stop. I'm not sure if I'm changing the dream or trying to shut it down.
I still kind of hate doing this because it feels fake, but fine, instead of freezing at the door I yell for my neighbor and grab a chair to jam under the knob so I can hold my ground.
I’m so scared my chest is tight, and instead of dealing with it I slide into the closet and stay completely still, hoping whoever is outside just goes away.
I take a breath and tell myself not to panic while I back away from the door, but the second the knob starts turning I give up and force myself awake before anything can happen.
I honestly don’t get how rewriting this is supposed to help, because what I want to do is just crawl under the bed and make myself disappear until the footsteps stop.
I’m terrified and my hands are shaking, but I slow my breathing, turn on the hallway light, and say through the door that they need to leave because I’m not backing away this time.
I steady myself first so I’m not spiraling, and then I call 911 and shout to the person outside that the police are on the way while I wedge the dresser against the door.
